references.text: The fundamental prohibition against shedding human blood, because humans are created in God's image. This establishes the theological basis for the commandment against murder.
Reiterates the prohibition against taking a human life and sets forth the death penalty as the consequence.
Detailed laws concerning homicide and manslaughter, which expand on the commandment by distinguishing between intentional murder and accidental killing.
Restatement of the sixth commandment in Deuteronomy, where Moses repeats the Ten Commandments to the people.
A curse upon anyone who kills their neighbor in secret, emphasizing the seriousness of the commandment.

Jesus expands on the commandment and teaches that not only murder, but also anger toward one's brother is subject to judgment. This extends the application of the commandment to the attitude of the heart.
Jesus quotes the commandment 'You shall not kill' as part of the path to eternal life.
Jesus mentions the commandment against murder in his conversation with the rich young man.
Jesus refers to the commandment against murder when speaking with the rich ruler.
Paul quotes the commandment against murder and explains that all commandments are summed up in the command to love.
James cites the commandment against murder to show that whoever breaks one commandment is guilty of breaking the whole law.
John teaches that anyone who hates their brother is a murderer. This links the commandment to the condition of the heart, in line with Jesus' teaching.
Direct quotation and theological reflection where Jesus challenges the understanding of 'you shall not kill'.
